backends.source: candidate before review, superseded contended cpuset 0-3

conditions.discarded_trials: A ladder that shared cpuset 8-11 with another unit's harness; a kimi comparison begun before the candidate source was final; a batch of rungs that ran after the fixture server was killed. All were repeated rather than reported.
conditions.fixture_restart: The fixture server was killed once mid-session and restarted from unchanged source, so the fixture revision is the same for every retained trial.
conditions.harness_arguments: defaults for --timeout (240) and --grace (10); no retained rung used a grace above the harness's 45-second watchdog margin
conditions.integrity: No retained rung recorded watchdog_killed, a cleanup survivor, a turn without a result, or a pidfd wait fallback.
conditions.orphans: Two processes of this unit's own, survivors of a batch killed when the fixture server died, sat in scopes pinned to 0-3 for about eighty minutes at near-zero CPU and were reaped before the final runs.
conditions.resource_group: /sys/fs/cgroup/hmzbench/u16 via hmzbench-in: cpuset.cpus 8-11 exclusive (cgroup v2 cpuset, not task affinity), cpu.max 400000/100000, memory.max 16 GiB, memory.swap.max 0. The harness recorded valid_4cpu_16gib true for every rung.
conditions.serialization: One run.py at a time; hmzbench-in refuses to start while the group holds a process.
conditions.speed_floor: Complete-turn latency, from turn submission to the result and startup included, at most 2x the serial control of the same source, for cold and warm p50 and p95 alike. Throughput is not the reading: N sessions always finish more work than one.
conditions.superseded_condition: Earlier figures from this unit were taken on cpuset 0-3 with taskset plus a systemd user scope, while sibling units' benchmarks held neighbouring quads. They are systematically pessimistic and are not reported. Every backend cleared a higher width once the cores were exclusive: claude 6 to 7, dsh 8 to 12, mimo 5 to 8, opencode 4 to 6.
conditions.validity_checks_retained: All items correct, a fresh execution proof per turn, immutable task inputs, the turn-two marker recalled from the conversation alone, exactly one result, at least one tool event, no cleanup survivors, no watchdog kill.

limitations: Synthetic loopback responses. No real-model throughput, provider limit or reasoning quality is established.

Kimi, mimo and opencode are confirmed widths rather than boundaries: the width above each was never tried. The run that would have tried mimo 9 and opencode 7 was stopped when this unit was asked to hand over.
Five-repeat groups pool more observations than five serial controls, so their p95 estimators carry different uncertainty.

Kimi's serial cold-startup control rose monotonically across five trials on this host, 17.7 to 28.1 to 38.4 to 43.1 to 55.1 seconds, while the CLI's own home grew past 265 MB and 3,900 files. No cause was established. Kimi rungs are comparable only to the serial controls taken beside them.

The kimi driver change's measured result is its call count against the shared daemon, 79 daemon calls per cold/warm task pair before and 43 after, taken from an instrumented probe rather than from these rungs. No timing improvement is claimed.
Mixed-backend concurrency is not measured here.
